title: Order Consolidation, Price Efficiency, and Extreme Liquidity Shocks
one_line: On quarterly S&P 500 futures expirations, index arbitrage sends large, predictable, mostly informationless order flow into S&P 500 stocks; the NYSE's consolidated opening handled it far more efficiently than Nasdaq (before its 2004 opening cross).

findings.statement: Index-arbitrage unwinds at quarterly expirations create large, predictable, informationless order flow.
Consolidated opening auctions price it more efficiently.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics at expiration (settlement-related order flow).
why.mechanism: Arbitrageurs unwind at the settlement print; consolidated auctions absorb it.

reported_results.headline: Witching-day order flow is large and predictable.

tradable_edge: Context for third_friday_spike_es: expiration-day flows are predictable; report quarterly (witching) expirations separately.
angles: Quarterly vs monthly expirations in the third-Friday test
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
